analysis.title: October 2026: First Look on Hedge Fund Performance and Positioning
key_insights: Global Fundamental L/S asset-weighted returns were -3.49% in October vs MSCI TR -0.77%, driven by both beta losses and negative alpha. YTD return is +9.1%.

Systematic L/S returned -3.6% in October, the largest monthly drawdown since November 2020 and the first down month since July 2025. The loss came entirely from negative long-side alpha. YTD return is +16.2%.
October was the first month on the desk's record (since 2016) in which both Fundamental L/S and Systematic L/S fell by 3% or more.
Global Fundamental L/S alpha was -1.75%, the worst monthly alpha since July and second worst in more than four years. Long-side losses drove it, with short-side losses a smaller factor.
Largest alpha detractors for Fundamental L/S were Volatility, China, Short-Term Momentum and Short Crowdedness. The United States, Health Care and Size partly offset them.
Largest alpha detractors for Systematic L/S were Short Crowdedness, Medium-Term Momentum and Asset Selection. Profitability, Earnings Yield and Growth partly offset them.
Asia L/S managers fell -9.4% in October, US L/S -1.9% and Europe L/S -0.5%. YTD, Asia is +14%, Europe +7.8% and US +6.4%.
TMT L/S funds lost -12.6% in October (+5.1% YTD). Health Care L/S funds lost -1.4% (+8.5% YTD).

Equal-weighted average Fundamental L/S return was -0.98% and the median -1.69%, against an asset-weighted -3.49%, which indicates larger managers underperformed. Dispersion between the 75th and 25th percentile was 10.44%.

Global equities saw the largest dollar net selling since March, driven by an equal amount of long and short sales. Single stocks were net sold on risk unwinds with long sales outpacing short sales 4 to 1. Macro products (index and ETF) were net bought, with long buys outpacing short sales 1.6 to 1.

Overall Prime Book net leverage fell 4.2 pts to 73.4% (9th percentile one-year), the fastest decline since March. Gross leverage rose 4.8 pts to 314.5% (86th percentile one-year), driven by mark-to-market.
Global Fundamental L/S net leverage fell 3.2 pts to 49.2% (3rd percentile one-year), led by reductions in Asia L/S funds. Asia Fundamental L/S net leverage fell 21.6 pts to 40.9%.
Every region except DM Asia was net sold in October, led by EM Asia and North America. Taiwan, Korea and China were all net sold in EM Asia.
Europe's weighting vs MSCI World ACWI rose 0.7 pts to 3.5% overweight, a 1-year high. North America's underweight vs MSCI World ACWI widened to 15.2% (rose 2.1 pts).

US Info Tech saw the largest dollar net selling since June, led by Tech Hardware, Semis and Semi Equipment, and IT Services. Software was the only subsector not net sold. US Info Tech long/short ratio is 1.71, in the 7th percentile vs the past five years.
US Materials saw the largest dollar net selling since May 2024. The US Materials long/short ratio is 1.77, in the 1st percentile vs the past five years.
Defensive sectors were net bought for the first time in 7 months, with Staples and Health Care both net bought. US Health Care was net bought for the first time in 3 months, driven by short covering.

ETF shorts make up 10.5% of the US equity short book excluding index products, up from 10.1% in September. That sits in the 18th percentile vs the past year and the 1st percentile vs the past five years.

sector_views.rationale: Hedge funds net sold US Info Tech most since June, mainly long sales. Long/short ratio is 1.71, in the 7th percentile vs five years.
Largest dollar net selling in US Materials since May 2024. Long/short ratio is 1.77, in the 1st percentile vs five years.
Net bought for the first time in 3 months on short covering, though long/short ratio of 2.40 is in the 6th percentile vs the past year.
Defensive sectors, including Staples, were net bought for the first time in 7 months.
Net sold for the first time in 4 months as short sales outpaced long buys 1.5 to 1. Long/short ratio is 2.73.

risk_factors: Crowded short positioning hurt both cohorts, as Short Crowdedness was a top alpha detractor for Fundamental and Systematic L/S.
Gross leverage near the 86th percentile one-year (97th percentile five-year) alongside low net leverage means large-manager de-grossing risk persists, per the figures reported.
Large managers underperformed in October (asset-weighted -3.49% vs simple average -0.98%), with wide return dispersion across funds.
vol_and_positioning: Overall Prime Book gross leverage is 314.5% (86th percentile one-year, 97th percentile five-year). Net leverage is 73.4% (9th percentile one-year). Long/short ratio is 1.609 (7th percentile one-year).
Global Fundamental L/S gross leverage is 210.7% (48th percentile one-year) and net leverage 49.2% (3rd percentile one-year). Long/short ratio is 1.610 (3rd percentile one-year).
US Fundamental L/S gross leverage rose 6.2 pts to 214.9% (59th percentile one-year). Net leverage rose 1.4 pts to 47.1% (8th percentile one-year). Long/short ratio is 1.562.
Europe Fundamental L/S gross leverage is 178.0%, net leverage 67.4% and long/short ratio 2.218. Asia Fundamental L/S gross leverage is 188.9%, net leverage 40.9% and long/short ratio 1.553.

Net selling by region: North America was net sold for a second straight month, with short sales outpacing long buys 3.5 to 1. EM Asia net selling was the largest since July, driven by long and short sales 2.5 to 1.
DM Asia was net bought as short covers outpaced long sales 4.2 to 1. Buying in Australia, Hong Kong and Singapore was partly offset by selling in Japan.
US Consumer Discretionary saw little net activity, with long sales offset by short covers, which points to de-grossing. Its long/short ratio is 2.01, in the 4th percentile vs the past year.

Most net sold US industries in October: Tech Hardware, Diversified Telecomm Svcs, Semis and Semi Equip, Oil Gas and Consumable Fuels, Broadline Retail, IT Services, Financial Services, Electronic Equip.
Most net bought US industries in October: Automobiles, Staples Distribution and Retail, Specialized REITs, Aerospace and Defense, Banks, Software, Specialty Retail, Construction Materials.
